Information a computer can save and use
The physical parts of a computer
Data is information — like numbers, words, and pictures — that a computer can save and use.
Instructions that tell a computer what to do
Code is instructions written in a special language that tell a computer exactly what to do, step by step.
A powerful computer that stores and shares information
A server is a powerful computer that keeps websites and apps running and sends information to other devices.
How does a robot know what to do?
It follows instructions programmed by a person
It thinks like a human brain
A robot does exactly what its code tells it to do. It follows instructions written by a programmer, step by step.
Saving and using files on the internet
A weather app on your phone
The cloud means your files are saved on computers connected to the internet, so you can access them from anywhere.
Making programs by connecting colorful blocks
Scratch lets you make programs, games, and animations by dragging and snapping colorful blocks together — no typing needed!
AI stands for Artificial Intelligence — computers that can learn and solve problems, a bit like how humans think.
How does a robot know what to do?
It thinks for itself like a human
Robots follow code — instructions written by a programmer that tell the robot exactly what to do and when.
What is the difference between data and information?
Data is raw unprocessed facts; information is data that has been given meaning
Data is stored on a hard drive; information is stored in the cloud
Data refers to raw facts and figures (e.g. numbers, text). Information is data that has been processed and given context, making it useful and meaningful.
What is the purpose of a function in programming?
To group reusable instructions that can be called multiple times
To store data permanently on the computer
A function is a named block of code that performs a specific task. By defining it once, you can call it multiple times throughout your program without repeating the same code.
In a client-server model, what does the client do?
It sends requests to the server and displays the responses
It stores all the websites and data
It runs the operating system for all connected devices
In a client-server model, the client (e.g. your browser) sends requests for data, and the server responds with the requested information. The server handles storage and processing.
What does \'autonomous\' mean when describing a robot?
The robot can operate and make decisions without constant human control
The robot needs a human to control every movement
The robot can only perform one pre-programmed task
An autonomous robot can sense its environment, process information, and make decisions on its own — without a human directing each action.
What is a key advantage of cloud computing for a datacenter?
Resources can be scaled up or down instantly based on demand
Data is stored physically closer to the user

Cloud computing allows datacenters to dynamically allocate resources. When demand spikes, more computing power can be added instantly — and reduced when not needed — making it highly flexible and efficient.
In Scratch, what programming concept does a \'repeat\' block represent?
A loop — a sequence of instructions that executes multiple times
A variable — a container that stores a value
An event — something that triggers a response
A \'repeat\' block is an example of a loop. Loops allow a set of instructions to run a specified number of times, avoiding the need to write the same code repeatedly.
How does a machine learning model improve its performance over time?
By analyzing large amounts of training data and adjusting its internal parameters
By being manually reprogrammed after each mistake
By randomly trying different approaches until one works
Machine learning models learn by processing large datasets. They adjust their internal parameters based on patterns they find, gradually improving accuracy without being explicitly reprogrammed.
What is the difference between a sensor and an actuator in a robot?
A sensor collects data from the environment; an actuator produces movement or output
A sensor controls the motors; an actuator reads the code
They perform the same function in different programming languages
Sensors are input devices that gather information (e.g. distance, light, color). Actuators are output devices that make the robot do something (e.g. motors, speakers, LEDs).
